subject: Request: temporary throughput carveout for Zenith Analytics go-live
messages:
From: Amelia Dawson <amelia@zenithanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput carveout for Zenith Analytics go-live

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. Quick follow-up: our go-live for the European tenant is scheduled for Monday 2 Nov at 08:00 CET and the first 24–48 hours are critical for our onboarding funnels. Based on our load tests we expect a 3–4x spike in short-lived inference requests (peak ~1.2M tokens/hour).

We want to request a temporary uplift to the burst/priority pool for the go-live window to avoid throttling and to keep 99th‑pct latency under 300ms. Specifically:
- Priority token pool for 48 hours starting 2026-11-02 07:00 CET
- Hard cap: additional 1.0M tokens per hour aggregated
- Fallback behavior: if exceeded, prefer graceful throttling rather than outright 429s

Can Redwood confirm whether this is possible, any cadence for approval, and the expected cost impact? We can sign an SLA appendix or short addendum if needed.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — this is blocking our launch checklist.

Best,
Amelia
Head of Platform, Zenith Analytics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Dawson <amelia@zenithanalytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput carveout for Zenith Analytics go-live

Hi Amelia — thanks for the details and the timeline. I’m looping in Vivek (ops) and Marissa (account lead) to scope an operational plan.

Initial thoughts: we can typically provision a temporary priority token pool for a short window, but anything beyond our standard 24‑hour burst carveout requires leadership approval and an SLA appendix. I’ll put together proposed caps, pricing, and rollback behavior and get back by tomorrow EOD PT.

Can you attach the load test summary and the peak-by-hour estimate? That will help our capacity team.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary throughput carveout for Zenith Analytics go-live

Team — forwarding Amelia's request. Key asks: 48h priority token pool, +1.0M tokens/hr hard cap, prefer graceful throttling vs 429, keep 99th‑pct latency < 300ms.

Proposed Redwood response (operational):
- Provision: priority token pool +1.0M tokens/hr for 48 hours starting 2026-11-02 07:00 CET
- Enforcement: hard aggregate cap; token accounting per customer; when pool exhausted revert to baseline fairness policies but route through a lower-cost model variant (faster model with higher quantization) as fallback
- Observability: 30s metrics, alert to oncall + customer, pre‑approved rollback script
- Billing: one‑time uplift fee equivalent to 20% of the estimated incremental token cost (we can bill as a credit/one-off charge on next invoice)
- Requirements: signed SLA Appendix C (attached), usage estimate CSV, and PO or billing approval

I attached the SLA exception form and a quick usage estimate I sketched (sla-exception-form.pdf, usage-estimate-zenith.csv). Please comment — need Vivek/Marissa signoff to commit.

— Soojin
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary throughput carveout for Zenith Analytics go-live

Thanks, Soojin. Reviewed the ask and the ops plan. I approve a temporary priority token pool but propose the following tighter constraints given capacity risk across EU region: 
- Limit window to 36 hours (2026-11-02 07:00 CET -> 2026-11-03 19:00 CET)
- Hard cap: +800k tokens/hr (not 1.0M) aggregated
- Billing: one‑time uplift fee = 15% of estimated incremental usage (we should give them a credit note option rather than deferring to open invoicing)
- SLA appendix must include automatic fallback to the compatible model variant and explicit rollback thresholds at 70% and 90% of the pool

Operational caveats: engineering needs an hour lead time to stage the priority pool and test the routing policy in canary. Marissa — please confirm commercial acceptability; Lauren — can you update the appendix & send to Amelia with DocuSign link?

If agreed, I’ll authorize ops to stage the config once DocuSign is returned.

— Vivek
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Dawson <amelia@zenithanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Approved: temporary priority pool for Zenith go‑live (terms & next steps)

Hi Amelia — good news: we can support a temporary priority pool for your go‑live with the following approved terms (please review and sign Appendix C via DocuSign):

Approved terms (summary):
- Window: 2026-11-02 07:00 CET -> 2026-11-03 19:00 CET (36 hours)
- Capacity: +800k tokens/hour aggregate priority pool
- Fallback: automatic graceful downgrade to a compatible model variant when thresholds hit; throttling thresholds at 70% and 90% of the pool with pre‑approved rollback actions
- Billing: one‑time uplift fee = 15% of the estimated incremental usage (we attached the usage estimate). We can invoice or apply as a credit — please indicate preference on the DocuSign form.
- Requirements: signed Appendix C (SLA exception form) and acceptance of rollback thresholds

Operational timeline:
- Please return the signed DocuSign link by EOD 2026-11-01 PT so our engineering team can stage the priority pool on 2026-11-02 06:00 CET for a 07:00 CET start.
- Our oncall will provide 30s telemetry and a dedicated Slack channel during the window.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/req/ZYX-8912
Attachments: sla-exception-form.pdf, usage-estimate-zenith.csv

If you’re OK, sign the DocuSign and I’ll confirm staging.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Dawson <amelia@zenithanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-eng@zenithanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approved: temporary priority pool for Zenith go‑live (terms & next steps)

Soojin — thanks, this looks good. We signed and returned Appendix C via DocuSign (signed copy attached by DocuSign). We prefer the credit option for billing.

A few quick notes: we’ll push a reduced-load canary at 06:45 CET and then ramp over 20 minutes; our platform team will monitor the Slack channel you mentioned. Please confirm once the pool is staged and give the ingestion runbook for the fallback model variant.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will report back after the initial ramp.

Best,
Amelia
Head of Platform, Zenith Analytics
